subject: Mutual Action Plan: prompt pack swap & usage covenant
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@shopfront.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-25T09:10:00-08:00
Subject: Dataset sharing and MAP for prompt evaluation (intro)

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Per our conversation, I put together a light mutual action plan to enable a short evaluation: Redwood will provide a prompt pack and a small curated dataset (ephemeral access) so your engineers can validate accuracy and latency on your shopper flows; Shopfront will provide a set of labeled test cases and a brief acceptance checklist.

High-level asks from us:
- Confirm the minimal set of current SKUs and sample user prompts you want included (we recommended 1,200 utterances).
- Confirm any strict usage constraints (retention window, export restrictions, on-premise only samples).

I attached a draft MAP schedule and the NDA you signed for reference. If the scope looks right I can circulate a ZIP with the prompt pack and a secure download link for the dataset (ephemeral, 14 days) — we can adjust the retention window if you need a shorter test window.

Next step: can we lock the MAP milestones this week? I propose: data exchange by 2026-03-02, QA sprint 1 week, acceptance review 2026-03-11.

Thanks —
Sean
Sean Gallagher
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: MAP_schedule.xlsx (spreadsheet)]
[Attachment: NDA_shopfront_signed.pdf (pdf)]

From: Elena Park <elena.park@shopfront.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@shopfront.com
Date: 2026-02-25T11:47:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dataset sharing and MAP for prompt evaluation (intro)

Sean —

Appreciate the clarity. A couple quick notes from our side:
- We can provide the labeled test cases (approx 850) but need to limit external export of customer-identifying fields. Can Redwood supply a schema for what you'll include in the sample so we can pre-mask sensitive fields?
- The 14-day ephemeral window is OK but procurement would prefer 7 days where feasible. Can you support both options (7d or 14d) depending on the dataset subset?
- We also require a simple usage covenant that prohibits reuse outside this evaluation and certifies deletion after the window.

Procurement is looped to confirm contract language, but from an engineering standpoint this is green. If you can share the prompt pack and the proposed covenant text, we'll review and get back with any redlines.

Best,
Elena Park
Head of Product, Shopfront Retail

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@shopfront.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-01T08:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dataset sharing and MAP for prompt evaluation (intro)

Elena —

Thanks — quick answers inline and attached a ZIP with the prompt pack and a proposed "evaluation covenant" doc.

- Schema: attached CSV schema (promptpack_schema.csv) included inside shopfront_promptpack_v1.zip. We will only include anonymized SKU ids and synthetic user identifiers unless you mark specific fields as non-exportable.
- Retention: we can support both strategies. By default we'll provision a 14-day secure download link; if you request a 7-day window for a subset, we can segregate artifacts and shorten the link TTL. Note that runtime logs tied to the trial (debug traces) will only be retained for 7 days unless you authorize longer for debugging.
- Covenant: the attached evaluation covenant contains the non-reuse clause, prohibition on redistribution, and a destruction attestation that a Shopfront engineer signs at the end of the trial.

Attachments in this message: shopfront_promptpack_v1.zip (prompt set + schema), MAP_schedule.xlsx (updated with separation between 7d/14d lanes), evaluation_covenant_v1.docx.

If procurement is okay we'll mark the data exchange milestone for 2026-03-02 (14d lane) with an optional 7d lane for the PII-restricted subset. Can we confirm the SKU list by EOD 2026-03-02?

Cheers,
Sean
[Attachment: shopfront_promptpack_v1.zip (zip)]
[Attachment: evaluation_covenant_v1.docx (docx)]

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-02T09:05:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: review of Shopfront MAP, constraints and escrow

Team — quick internal note before we finalize:

- Confirm enforceability: procurement may request that the covenant requires a third-party attestation. We should propose our standard deletion webhook that triggers a signed confirmation (we have an automation for that).
- Quota & throttling: set a soft rate-limit for the evaluation endpoints to soak at expected traffic (we recommend 10 r/s during the QA sprint).
- Escrow of prompts: because Shopfront is providing labeled cases, let's keep a copy in our secure sandbox for audit only and ensure it is flagged ephemeral with a 14-day lifecycle. No derivative use for model updates.

Action items: Sean to confirm the SKU list with Elena; Marissa to prepare the deletion webhook snippet and Connor to provision the ephemeral bucket with 7d/14d lanes.

Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Customer Success, Redwood Inference

From: Elena Park <elena.park@shopfront.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, procurement@shopfront.com
Date: 2026-03-03T16:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan: prompt pack swap & usage covenant

Sean/All —

Procurement approved the covenant with two minor redlines: shorten the default runtime log retention to 3 days and add a clause that Shopfront must receive the signed deletion attestation within 48 hours of the TTL expiry. Otherwise we're good to proceed.

We've attached the SKU list in a separate secure upload (sent to your download link). We'll take the 7-day lane for the PII-restricted subset and the 14-day lane for the synthetic test set.

Please confirm you received the upload and provisioning timeline so we can sync QA timelines.

Thanks —
Elena
Head of Product, Shopfront Retail
[Attachment referenced: SKU_list_upload (secure link)]
